original_question: Let (T (t))t≥0 be a contraction semigroup with generator A on a Hilbert space H. Consider the following properties: (i) There exists m ≥ 0 such that k(λ − A)xk ≥ m| Re λ|kxk for all Re λ < 0 and all x ∈ H. (ii) There exists m1 > 0 such that kT (t)xk ≥ m1 kxk for all t ≥ 0, x ∈ H. Does assertion (i) imply assertion (ii)?
correct_elements: Your draft clearly targets the right place in the paper and reproduces the official problem almost verbatim: the setting is a contraction semigroup on a Hilbert space with generator A, property (i) is a resolvent-type lower estimate, property (ii) is a uniform lower bound for the semigroup, and the implication being asked is exactly the one posed in the paper.
missing_details: The paper is asking this as an open problem in Section 7, Problem 26, not as a proved theorem or conjecture.
Because A is called the generator, the intended object is a C0-semigroup; strong continuity is implicit from the paper’s global C0-semigroup framework.
As printed, condition (i) says the estimate holds for all x ∈ H, but to make the expression (λ − A)x well-defined one must read this as x ∈ D(A).
As printed, condition (i) uses m ≥ 0; to make the question non-vacuous and consistent with the surrounding comment that it is still open, the intended constant must be strictly positive, m > 0.
The nearby context records that (ii) implies (i), that the analogous implication is false for merely bounded semigroups, and that Batty notes the question was still open as of April 2021.
refined_question: Let (T(t))t≥0 be a C0-contraction semigroup on a Hilbert space H with generator A. Suppose there exists a constant m > 0 such that ||(λ − A)x|| ≥ m|Re λ|·||x|| for every λ ∈ C with Re λ < 0 and every x ∈ D(A). Must there then exist a constant m1 > 0 such that ||T(t)x|| ≥ m1||x|| for every t ≥ 0 and every x ∈ H?
justification: The draft is aiming at Section 7, Problem 26 (Lower bounds), page 19, and it matches the printed formulation very closely. I kept the scope exactly there. I only made the question self-contained by making the implicit C0-assumption explicit and by repairing two apparent slips in the printed display: if m were allowed to be 0, then (i) would be trivial, which is incompatible with the surrounding statement that this is an open question; and if x were allowed to range over all of H, then (λ − A)x would not be well-typed. The surrounding comment on page 19 is the right nearby context and confirms that the intended issue is precisely whether the resolvent lower bound forces a uniform semigroup lower bound.
